description: 3,643 restaurants carry no cuisine label. Cuisine is the primary dimension of the Market Overview, so these gaps bias every category statistic.
recommended_action: Fill with an explicit 'UNKNOWN' rather than dropping, so the denominator stays honest, and state the exclusion wherever category shares are quoted.

description: 3,641 rows use 1900-01-01 as a placeholder. These rows have null ACTION, SCORE and VIOLATION, and the 3,641 restaurants involved appear nowhere else in the table — i.e. permitted but never-yet-inspected establishments, not corrupted dates.
recommended_action: Must be excluded from any trend or score analysis (otherwise the time axis stretches back to 1900), but retained for market-size counts — these are real, operating restaurants.

description: 3,048 rows carry (0, 0) coordinates, which would plot off the coast of Africa. Their BORO and address fields are intact — only geocoding is missing. A further 0 rows fall outside the NYC bounding box.
recommended_action: Convert (0,0) to NaN — it must never be treated as a valid location. Exclude from map layers while keeping the rows in borough-level statistics.

description: 17,125 rows have no score; 13,484 of those have a non-null ACTION, meaning the inspection did occur but the score is absent.
recommended_action: Do NOT fill with 0 — a score of 0 means 'flawless' and would understate risk badly. Keep NaN and average over de-duplicated inspection-level scores.

description: 1,701 rows have no coordinates and cannot be mapped.
recommended_action: Exclude from map layers only; non-spatial cuisine and score analysis is unaffected. Optional fallback: ZIPCODE centroids.

description: 150 rows are exact duplicates across all 27 fields. The count matches the business-key duplicate count exactly, so these are pure re-entries with no hidden differences.
recommended_action: Drop with drop_duplicates(), keeping the first. Very low risk.

description: Capitalisation is in fact consistent — every value is standard Title Case ("Manhattan"), with no "MANHATTAN"/"manhattan" variants. The actual defect is 372 rows holding the placeholder "0", which is not a real borough.
recommended_action: Map to "Unknown". Note that these rows have NO coordinates at all (0 usable), so a spatial join against the boundary file cannot recover them; only a ZIPCODE lookup could.

description: Text fields carry casing and whitespace noise: normalising DBA collapses 82 duplicate trade names, and 39,344 STREET values contain consecutive spaces. Both break chain-brand identification and address matching.
recommended_action: Strip, collapse internal whitespace, uppercase. Retain the original trade name in a separate column for traceability.

description: 1,907 rows score above 100 (max 214). DOHMH scores have no upper bound, and 75% of these records carry a closure order versus 4% overall — so most are genuine extreme violations, not entry errors.
recommended_action: Do not delete. Keep the raw value and add a winsorized column (99th percentile) for charting, so means are not dragged by the tail.

description: The boundary file is complete (5 rows, no missing values) and BoroName joins directly to the inspection data's BORO. The only defect: area and length carry thousands separators and are therefore parsed as strings rather than numbers.
recommended_action: Strip commas and cast to float on load; parse the_geom with shapely.wkt.loads for mapping.

description: Over 50% of records carry no grade. Cross-tabulation confirms this follows DOHMH policy: only Cycle and Pre-permit inspections are graded. Not a data entry problem.
recommended_action: Keep as NaN, do not impute. Restrict grade-distribution analysis to gradeable inspection types so the denominator stays correct.

description: Consistency check passes: BORO, CUISINE, DBA and ZIPCODE never conflict across the rows of a single CAMIS (0 conflicts in total). Restaurant master data is reliable and can safely be aggregated by CAMIS.
recommended_action: No action needed. When building the restaurant dimension table, any row's attributes will do — no conflict resolution required.
